jobs.title: Geologist 9-P11/12 - Kalamazoo District Office
jobs.description:
Job Description

This position serves as the senior level geological/hydrogeological expert for the Materials Management Division (MMD) in the Kalamazoo District. The position is responsible for all aspects of Part 115, Solid Waste Management, of the Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act, 1994 PA 451, as amended (NREPA), and the pursuant promulgated administrative rules. This position is responsible for conducting technical reviews on all incoming landfill construction permit applications, including review of the hydrogeologic studies and monitoring plans submitted to support these applications. For those landfills in the process of investigating or remediation of contaminated groundwater, this position evaluates investigation reports, remedial action plans, and monitoring data submitted to demonstrate and support remedial action selection and performance This position inspects solid waste disposal facilities and evaluates all groundwater, leachate, surface water, and gas monitoring results to determine compliance with Part 115 requirements. This position inspects unlicensed or illegal sites where solid waste is disposed. Sampling is conducted to provide oversight of sampling techniques at facilities, assure the integrity of submitted results, and to collect data in support of remedial investigations and enforcement actions. Expert hydrogeologic witness testimony may be required. Hydrogeologic support and expertise in support of compliance and enforcement activity is provided.

Position Description (9-P11)

Position Description (12)

Required Education And Experience

Education

Possession of a bachelor's degree in geology or geological, petroleum or mining engineering.

Experience

Geologist 9

No specific type or amount is required.

Geologist 10

One year of professional experience in carrying out geological activities to protect, develop and maintain natural resources equivalent to a Geologist 9.

Geologist P11

Two years of professional experience in carrying out geological activities to protect, develop and maintain natural resources equivalent to a Geologist, including one year equivalent to a Geologist 10.

Geologist 12

Three years of professional experience in carrying out geological activities to protect, develop and maintain natural resources equivalent to a Geologist, including one year equivalent to Geologist P11.

Alternate Education And Experience

Possession of a bachelor's degree in environmental geoscience, earth science, or environmental science with 15 semester (23 quarter term) credits in the following core geology classes: physical geology, sedimentology/stratigraphy, mineralogy/petrology, structural geology and field instruction. In addition, the candidate must have 21 semester (32 quarter term) credits in elective geology coursework; and two courses each in calculus, chemistry and physics.

About Egle

Additional Requirements and Information

The Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy's mission is to protect Michigan’s environment and public health by managing air, water, land, and energy resources.

View the class specification at: http://www.michigan.gov/documents/Geologist_12698_7.pdf

Accommodations

If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or selection processes, please contact the ADA coordinator for the agency that posted this position vacancy.

Position Overview

Davey Resource Group, a Davey Company, has opportunities for an experienced Environmental Scientist/ Restoration Specialist. Davey Resource Group is a leader in the natural resource and forestry consulting industries throughout the US.

Job Duties

The Environmental Specialist will provide our government, utility, commercial, private and not-for-profit clients with the services and solutions needed to efficiently and effectively manage natural resources and comply with policies.

Selected candidates will work collaboratively as part of a team. Applicants should be willing to lead and train fellow team members on all aspects of field work. Position involves a variety of work, including invasive plant species control, native plant and seed installation, shoreline stabilization, and native habitat restoration (prairie, wetland and woodland).

The majority of work is outdoors, often in inclement weather and in rugged terrain, and may involve using heavy equipment, such as spray rigs, backpack sprayers, augers, chain saws, mowers, etc.

Work with the project manager to understand the contract needs and specifications of clients and their customers and develop appropriate solutions.

Experience with heavy equipment operation including skid steers, dingos, and tractors.
Experience with native plant installation, seeding, and erosion control best management practices.
Ability to work independently when not leading crews.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Coordinate the build. Track the moving pieces. Keep the project on course.

As a Project Coordinator – Grant Engineering & Construction, at Stimulus Technologies, you’ll support the planning and execution of large-scale fiber builds by tracking engineering deliverables, permitting progress, and construction activity across multiple partners. You’ll work directly with project and construction leadership to ensure designs are delivered, permits are moving, and contractors stay aligned with the overall project schedule, especially on grant-funded projects where timing and documentation are critical.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing complex workflows and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned. You’ll track milestones across design, permitting, and construction, follow up with engineering firms and contractors on key deliverables, and help ensure everything is documented and audit ready. If you’re organized, proactive, and interested in the behind-the-scenes coordination that keeps large infrastructure projects moving, this is a strong opportunity to build experience in engineering and construction project delivery.

Essential Functions

Schedule and Deliverable Tracking

Maintain and update the master project schedule for Grant-funded projects under the direction of the Project Manager, tracking design, permitting, construction, and turnover milestones.
Track engineering firm deliverables including HLD, MLD, construction-ready design packages, permitting submittals, and as-built documentation against agreed-upon schedules.
Track construction contractor progress including mainline build, splicing, testing, and closeout activities against the project schedule.
Flag overdue or at-risk deliverables and milestone dates to the Project Manager and Construction Manager proactively.
Maintain project dashboards showing schedule performance, deliverable status, and construction completion percentages for internal leadership and client reporting.
Track and log all change orders, scope modifications, and schedule revisions with supporting documentation.

Engineering Firm and Contractor Coordination

Coordinate information flow between the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Permitting Manager, engineering firm, and construction contractors.
Follow up with the engineering firm on outstanding design deliverables, permitting submittals, inspection reports, and as-built packages.
Follow up with construction contractors on daily production logs, pay application documentation, and closeout deliverables.
Route submittals, RFIs, design review comments, and approval requests to the appropriate parties and track response timelines.
Schedule and coordinate project meetings including weekly construction calls, design review sessions, and client status meetings; prepare agendas and capture meeting minutes and action items.
Maintain a running action item log across all project stakeholders and follow up on open items to drive closure.

Budget and Invoice Management

Process and log invoices from the engineering firm, construction contractors, pole owners, and permitting agencies; verify amounts against contracts, SOWs, and approved change orders.
Route invoices through the approval workflow and track payment status.
Track project expenditures against budgets and assist the Project Manager with variance reporting and cost forecasting.
Ensure all expenditures are properly categorized and documented to support Grant reimbursement submissions.
Assist with preparing cost summaries and budget reports for internal leadership and client reporting.

Grant Compliance and Documentation

Maintain organized, auditable project records in accordance with Grant program requirements, including schedules, budgets, invoices, deliverable logs, change orders, and correspondence.
Assist the Project Manager with preparation and submission of Grant progress reports, milestone certifications, and compliance documentation on schedule.
Compile construction production data, engineering deliverable status, and supporting documentation for grant reimbursement requests.
Track Grant reporting deadlines and ensure all required submissions are prepared and reviewed before due dates.
Maintain familiarity with Grant program rules, reporting templates, and compliance requirements; flag potential compliance risks to the Project Manager.
Support audit preparation by ensuring project files are complete, organized, and readily accessible.

Construction Documentation Support

Collect and consolidate daily and weekly construction production reports from the Construction Manager and engineering firm.
Update construction progress trackers with current data on route miles, strand miles, splicing, testing, and make-ready completion.
Track permitting status in coordination with the Permitting Manager; update the project schedule when new approvals or rejections affect the construction sequence.
Maintain organized files for construction documentation including inspection reports, daily logs, material delivery records, and contractor correspondence.
Prepare construction progress summaries for the Project Manager highlighting trends, variances, and areas requiring attention.

Education and Experience

Required

High school diploma or GED; associate or bachelor’s degree preferred.
Minimum 2 years of experience in project coordination, administrative support, or operations support, preferably in telecom, broadband, construction, or engineering.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Experience with project tracking tools or scheduling software (e.g., Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or equivalent).
Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple concurrent tracking streams and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across internal teams, external partners, and clients.
Ability to work independently and proactively follow up on open items without constant direction.
Travel up to ten percent.

Preferred

Experience supporting project management in telecom, broadband, or utility construction environments.
Familiarity with OSP fiber optic construction terminology, project phases, and deliverables (HLD, MLD, as-builts, splicing, testing).
Experience with BEAD, RDOF, ReConnect, CAF, or other government-funded broadband deployment programs.
Experience with grant compliance documentation, reporting, and reimbursement processes.
Familiarity with invoice processing, budget tracking, and basic cost reporting.
CAPM certification or coursework toward PMP.

Alignment with Core Values

At Stimulus Technologies, our core values define how we work. The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

Driven to Grow – Continuously seeks to develop professionally, stays current with industry practices, and pushes to improve processes and outcomes.
See a Need – Fill a Need – Proactively identifies gaps, obstacles, or opportunities and takes action without waiting to be asked.
Elevate Others – Mentors teammates, shares knowledge freely, and actively contributes to a positive and collaborative work environment.
Extreme Ownership – Takes full accountability for results, decisions, and mistakes; does not deflect blame or make excuses.
Celebrate Success – Recognizes contributions of team members, acknowledges milestones, and fosters a culture where wins are shared.

Management reserves the right to amend and change responsibilities to meet business and organizational needs as necessary.

Job Description

This position serves as the senior level geological/hydrogeological expert for the Materials Management Division (MMD) in the Kalamazoo District. This position is responsible for conducting technical reviews on all incoming landfill construction permit applications, including review of the hydrogeologic studies and monitoring plans submitted to support these applications. For those landfills in the process of investigating or remediation of contaminated groundwater, this position evaluates investigation reports, remedial action plans, and monitoring data submitted to demonstrate and support remedial action selection and performance This position inspects solid waste disposal facilities and evaluates all groundwater, leachate, surface water, and gas monitoring results to determine compliance with Part 115 requirements. This position inspects unlicensed or illegal sites where solid waste is disposed. Sampling is conducted to provide oversight of sampling techniques at facilities, assure the integrity of submitted results, and to collect data in support of remedial investigations and enforcement actions. Expert hydrogeologic witness testimony may be required. Hydrogeologic support and expertise in support of compliance and enforcement activity is provided.

As a Project Coordinator – Grant Engineering & Construction, at Stimulus Technologies, you’ll support the planning and execution of large-scale fiber builds by tracking engineering deliverables, permitting progress, and construction activity across multiple partners. You’ll work directly with project and construction leadership to ensure designs are delivered, permits are moving, and contractors stay aligned with the overall project schedule, especially on grant-funded projects where timing and documentation are critical.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys managing complex workflows and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned. You’ll track milestones across design, permitting, and construction, follow up with engineering firms and contractors on key deliverables, and help ensure everything is documented and audit ready. If you’re organized, proactive, and interested in the behind-the-scenes coordination that keeps large infrastructure projects moving, this is a strong opportunity to build experience in engineering and construction project delivery.

Essential Functions

Schedule and Deliverable Tracking

Maintain and update the master project schedule for Grant-funded projects under the direction of the Project Manager, tracking design, permitting, construction, and turnover milestones.
Track engineering firm deliverables including HLD, MLD, construction-ready design packages, permitting submittals, and as-built documentation against agreed-upon schedules.
Track construction contractor progress including mainline build, splicing, testing, and closeout activities against the project schedule.
Flag overdue or at-risk deliverables and milestone dates to the Project Manager and Construction Manager proactively.
Maintain project dashboards showing schedule performance, deliverable status, and construction completion percentages for internal leadership and client reporting.
Track and log all change orders, scope modifications, and schedule revisions with supporting documentation.

Engineering Firm and Contractor Coordination

Coordinate information flow between the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Permitting Manager, engineering firm, and construction contractors.
Follow up with the engineering firm on outstanding design deliverables, permitting submittals, inspection reports, and as-built packages.
Follow up with construction contractors on daily production logs, pay application documentation, and closeout deliverables.
Route submittals, RFIs, design review comments, and approval requests to the appropriate parties and track response timelines.
Schedule and coordinate project meetings including weekly construction calls, design review sessions, and client status meetings; prepare agendas and capture meeting minutes and action items.
Maintain a running action item log across all project stakeholders and follow up on open items to drive closure.

Budget and Invoice Management

Process and log invoices from the engineering firm, construction contractors, pole owners, and permitting agencies; verify amounts against contracts, SOWs, and approved change orders.
Route invoices through the approval workflow and track payment status.
Track project expenditures against budgets and assist the Project Manager with variance reporting and cost forecasting.
Ensure all expenditures are properly categorized and documented to support Grant reimbursement submissions.
Assist with preparing cost summaries and budget reports for internal leadership and client reporting.

Grant Compliance and Documentation

Maintain organized, auditable project records in accordance with Grant program requirements, including schedules, budgets, invoices, deliverable logs, change orders, and correspondence.
Assist the Project Manager with preparation and submission of Grant progress reports, milestone certifications, and compliance documentation on schedule.
Compile construction production data, engineering deliverable status, and supporting documentation for grant reimbursement requests.
Track Grant reporting deadlines and ensure all required submissions are prepared and reviewed before due dates.
Maintain familiarity with Grant program rules, reporting templates, and compliance requirements; flag potential compliance risks to the Project Manager.
Support audit preparation by ensuring project files are complete, organized, and readily accessible.

Construction Documentation Support

Collect and consolidate daily and weekly construction production reports from the Construction Manager and engineering firm.
Update construction progress trackers with current data on route miles, strand miles, splicing, testing, and make-ready completion.
Track permitting status in coordination with the Permitting Manager; update the project schedule when new approvals or rejections affect the construction sequence.
Maintain organized files for construction documentation including inspection reports, daily logs, material delivery records, and contractor correspondence.
Prepare construction progress summaries for the Project Manager highlighting trends, variances, and areas requiring attention.

Required

Minimum 2 years of experience in project coordination, administrative support, or operations support, preferably in telecom, broadband, construction, or engineering.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook.

Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple concurrent tracking streams and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across internal teams, external partners, and clients.

Company Overview

Company Overview

Devereux is one of the nation’s largest nonprofit organizations, providing services, insight and leadership in the evolving field of behavioral healthcare. Founded in 1912, Devereux operates a comprehensive national network of clinical, therapeutic, educational and employment programs that positively impact the lives of 10,000+ children, adults – and their families – every year.

Our Mission:
Devereux changes lives – by unlocking and nurturing human potential for people living with emotional, behavioral or cognitive differences.

With nearly 6,500 employees working in programs across the country, Devereux is a trusted partner for families, schools and communities, serving individuals in the areas of autism, intellectual and developmental disabilities, specialty mental health, education and foster care.

Our Culture, Our Expectations

At Devereux, Servant Leadership is embedded throughout our culture and every aspect of our organizational framework. Our mission-driven, people-first mindset is at the heart of the compassionate and high-quality programming we provide – every day – for the individuals and families we serve, and other key stakeholders. Devereux offers challenging and exciting work, and our team environment creates an empowering, positive and rewarding atmosphere. To be successful at Devereux, you will: put the needs of others first, feel called to serve and called to lead. As a member of our team, you will be a significant part of our commitment to providing a welcoming and supportive work environment across all programs and services, and within all policies and employee practices.

We believe a workplace rooted in inclusivity – offering a sense of belonging to all those who walk through our doors – is fundamental to delivering the highest quality healthcare services. Through open dialogue and the creation of brave spaces, we will engage in work that gives each of us a chance to change the world – one person, one family, one community at a time.

What Devereux Offers You

Employee assistance / work-life balance program.
